subject: Commit banding and reseller netback scenario planning for Quantum Retail
messages:
From: Felicia Gomez <felicia@quantumretail.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@quantumretail.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing split questions for private offer / reseller flow

Hi Lukas / Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement had two follow-ups before we build the PO: 1) how will list-price / discounting work at the private-offer level vs what our resellers will see, and 2) can you show a simple netback example that includes marketplace fees + reseller commission? Our CFO wants to understand how the committed-band tiers translate to the partner margin we plan to pass along.

Specifically: if we commit to $600k ARR year 1 with a 12% private-offer discount, and then give our reseller a 20% rebate on invoiced list price, what does Redwood expect to show as the partner netback after AWS marketplace fee and any pass-through? We also need to know whether commit banding (tiered list discounts) will be honored on the reseller side or fixed to the private-offer table.

Can you provide a short scenario spreadsheet and note if tax/withholding is treated on the invoice or on the reseller settlement?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement would like something by EOD Friday so we can include it in our approval packet.

Best,
Felicia Gomez
Head of Strategic Procurement
Quantum Retail

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing split questions for private offer / reseller flow

Hi Felicia —

Thanks — we can definitely walk through a few scenarios. Quick answers up front:
- Private-offer discount applies to the listing that Quantum accepts; resellers can still be paid a commission based on list price or net revenue depending on the chosen pass-through mechanism.
- Marketplace fees (AWS listing fee, 20% example) are taken at the marketplace settlement layer unless you elect programmatic passback; that impacts reseller netback if the reseller is paid on gross list.
- Commit banding for the private offer can be configured to be independent of reseller commissions (we've had customers keep list tiers separate and pay resellers a flat percentage).

I'll attach a simple workbook that models three scenarios: reseller paid on list price, reseller paid on net after marketplace fees, and reseller paid on Redwood net after our commission. See the attached "marketplace_fee_and_netback_scenarios.xlsx".

Action items: Ben / Irene — can you review the workbook and confirm the recommended standard we should propose for QRT? Specific asks from procurement: tax handling guidance and whether we can automate reseller pass-through in AWS private offers.

Thanks — I can also hop on a 30-min call if useful.

— Lukas
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: marketplace_fee_and_netback_scenarios.xlsx (stub); commit-banding-proposal.txt (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing split questions for private offer / reseller flow

Looping in Karthik for ops/marketplace specifics. Quick notes after scanning the workbook:
- Scenario A (reseller on list): Partner netback = list * (1 - reseller_pct) - marketplace_fee. Example row: list $1,000, reseller 20% = $200, AWS fee 12% = $120, partner netback = $1,000 - $200 - $120 = $680.
- Scenario B (reseller on net after marketplace fee): partner gets (list - marketplace_fee) * (1 - reseller_pct). Same numbers: ($1,000 - $120) * 0.8 = $704. Slightly higher for partner in this case.
- We should clarify where tax sits — standard is marketplace handles sales tax on the listing; reseller commissions are grossed and then treated per reseller agreement.

I recommend we propose option B to Quantum Retail: pay reseller on net-after-marketplace-fee. It preserves clearer accounting for both sides and avoids double-dipping when marketplace withholds fees.

Irene — can you confirm whether AWS private offer tooling supports automated pass-through of marketplace fee calculation to the reseller settlement? If not, we'll need to run a manual settlement schedule monthly.

Ben
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jul 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing split questions for private offer / reseller flow

Ben — confirmed: AWS marketplace will not automatically split reseller commission out of the AWS settlement in standard private-offer flows. Two practical paths:

1) Programmatic passback: We create a separate settlement flow where we invoice the reseller/netback line items and programmatically passback funds. This requires manual reconciliation initially and a small integration for automated reporting.

2) Redwood-managed settlement: Redwood invoices Quantum at net-of-discount; we remit reseller commission per the partner agreement (monthly). This is simplest from a tooling perspective but requires Redwood to act as the paying agent.

For QRT (given the size and timeline), I suggest option 2 for the initial year; it reduces complexity on the procurement side. We'll include a reconciliation appendix in the MA.

I attached a short commit-banding-proposal.txt that maps bands -> discounts and the recommended reseller handling (flat % by tier).

Irene
Head of Marketplace Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing split questions for private offer / reseller flow

Felicia —

Per our internal review, attached workbook + the recommendation below for the packet:

1) We modelled your $600k ARR commit at three bandings (0-300k, 300-750k, 750k+) and applied a 12% private-offer discount at contract signature.
2) Recommendation: pay resellers on net-after-marketplace-fee (scenario B). This yields a clearer settlement path and slightly higher partner netback vs paying on list.
3) For the first year, Redwood will act as the paying agent for reseller commissions and include a monthly reconciliation schedule in the MA. This avoids custom AWS marketplace plumbing during onboarding.
4) Tax: Marketplace will collect sales tax on the listing. Reseller commissions will be reported and grossed per the reseller's tax jurisdiction; Redwood will provide required 1099/withholding docs.

I've attached: Quantum_Retail_MA_v3_redline.pdf (we marked a short appendix for reseller settlement), marketplace_fee_and_netback_scenarios.xlsx, commit-banding-proposal.txt.

If that works, can procurement confirm acceptance of the Redwood-managed settlement approach and we'll add the language to the MA and issue PO guidance? Happy to do a 20-min call Monday to finalize.

Thanks,
Lukas
Senior Sales Lead
Redwood Inference
